1.e: Now (follow) the ceremonies (the knowledge of) which is derived from practice (and not from the Sruti).
They should be performed during the northern course of the sun, on days of the first fortnight (of the month), on auspicious days,
With the sacrificial cord suspended over (the sacrificer's) left shoulder.
(The rites should be performed) from left to right.
The beginning should be made on the east side or on the north side,
And also the end.
Ceremonies belonging to the Fathers (are performed) in the second fortnight (of the month),
With the sacrificial cord suspended over the right shoulder,
From right to left,
Ending in the south.
Ceremonies occasioned by special occurrences (are performed) according as their occasions demand.
Having set the fire in a blaze, he strews eastward-pointed Darbha grass around it,
Or eastward-pointed and northward-pointed (grass);
Southward-pointed at sacrifices to the Fathers,
Or southward-pointed and eastward-pointed.

1.s: uttareṇāgniṃ darbhāntsaṃstīrya dvandvaṃ nyañci pātrāṇi prayunakti devasaṃyuktāni |
1.d: उत्तरेणाग्निं दर्भान्त्संस्तीर्य द्वन्द्वं न्यञ्चि पात्राणि प्रयुनक्ति देवसंयुक्तानि ।
1.e: To the north of the fire he strews Darbha grass and (on that) he places the vessels (required for sacrifice) upside-down, two by two, if referring to ceremonies directed to the gods,
All at once, if to men,
One by one, if to the Fathers.

1.s: pavitrayossaṃkāra āyāmataḥ parīmāṇaṃ prokṣaṇīsaṃskāraḥ pātraprokṣa iti darśapūrṇamāsavattūṣṇīm |
1.d: पवित्रयोस्संकार आयामतः परीमाणं प्रोक्षणीसंस्कारः पात्रप्रोक्ष इति दर्शपूर्णमासवत्तूष्णीम् ।
1.e: The preparation of the (blades used as) 'purifiers,' the measure of their length, the preparation of the Prokshani water, and the sprinkling of the vessels are the same here as at the sacrifices of the new and full moon, (but are performed) in silence.

1.s: apareṇāgniṃ pavitrāntarhite pātre 'pa ānīyodagagrābhyāṃ pavitrābhyāṃ trirutpūya samaṃ prāṇairhṛtvottareṇāgniṃ darbheṣu sādayitvā darbhaiḥ pracchādya |
1.d: अपरेणाग्निं पवित्रान्तर्हिते पात्रे ऽप आनीयोदगग्राभ्यां पवित्राभ्यां त्रिरुत्पूय समं प्राणैर्हृत्वोत्तरेणाग्निं दर्भेषु सादयित्वा दर्भैः प्रच्छाद्य ।
1.e: To the west of the fire he pours water into a vessel over which he has laid (two grass blades called) purifiers, purifies (the water) three times with two northward-pointed purifiers, holds it on a level with his nose and mouth, places it to the north of the fire on Darbha grass, and covers it with Darbha grass.
On the south side he causes a Brahmana to sit down on Darbha grass.

1.s: ājyaṃ vilāpyāpareṇāgniṃ pavitrāntarhitāyāmājyasthālyāmājyaṃ nirūpyodīco 'ṅgārānnirūhya teṣvadhiśritya jvalatāvadyutya dve darbhāgre pratyasya triḥ paryagni kṛtvodagudvāsyāṅgārān pratyūhyodagagrābhyāṃ pavitrābhyāṃ punarāhāraṃ trirutpūya paritre anuprahṛtya |
1.d: आज्यं विलाप्यापरेणाग्निं पवित्रान्तर्हितायामाज्यस्थाल्यामाज्यं निरूप्योदीचो ऽङ्गारान्निरूह्य तेष्वधिश्रित्य ज्वलतावद्युत्य द्वे दर्भाग्रे प्रत्यस्य त्रिः पर्यग्नि कृत्वोदगुद्वास्याङ्गारान् प्रत्यूह्योदगग्राभ्यां पवित्राभ्यां पुनराहारं त्रिरुत्पूय परित्रे अनुप्रहृत्य ।
1.e: He melts the Agya, pours it, to the west of the fire, into the Agya-pot, over which he has laid two purifiers, draws coals (out of the sacrificial fire) towards the mirth, puts (the Agya) on them, throws light on it by means of a burning (grass-blade), throws two Darbha points into it, moves a firebrand round it three times, takes it from the fire towards the north, sweeps the coals back (into the fire), purifies (the Agya) three times with two northward-pointed purifiers, moving them backward and forward, and throws the purifiers into the fire.

2.s: yena juhoti tadagnau pratitapya darbhaiḥ saṃmṛjya punaḥ pratitapya prokṣya nidhāya darbhānadbhissaṃspṛśyāgnau praharati |
2.d: येन जुहोति तदग्नौ प्रतितप्य दर्भैः संमृज्य पुनः प्रतितप्य प्रोक्ष्य निधाय दर्भानद्भिस्संस्पृश्याग्नौ प्रहरति ।
2.e: He warms at the fire the implement with which he sacrifices, wipes it off with Darbha blades, warms it again, sprinkles it (with water), puts it down, touches the Darbha blades with water, and throws them into the fire.

As paridhis (or pieces of wood laid round the fire) yoke-pins are used at the marriage, the Upanayana, the Samavartana, the parting of the (wife's) hair, the tonsure of the child's hair, the cutting of the beard, and at expiatory ceremonies.

2.s: agniṃ pariṣiñcatyadite 'numanyasve ti dakṣiṇataḥ pracīna manumate 'numanyasveti paścādudīcīnaṃ sarasvate 'numanyasve tyuttarataḥ prācīnaṃ deva savitaḥ prasuve ti samantam |
2.d: अग्निं परिषिञ्चत्यदिते ऽनुमन्यस्वे ति दक्षिणतः प्रचीन मनुमते ऽनुमन्यस्वेति पश्चादुदीचीनं सरस्वते ऽनुमन्यस्वे त्युत्तरतः प्राचीनं देव सवितः प्रसुवे ति समन्तम् ।
2.e: He sprinkles water round the fire, on the south side from west to east with (the words), 'Aditi, give thy consent!' on the west side from south to north with 'Anumati, give thy consent!' on the north side from west to east with 'Sarasvati [sic], give thy consent!' all around with 'God Savitri, give thy impulse!'
At ceremonies belonging to the Fathers (water is sprinkled) only all round (the fire), silently.
Having put a piece of wood on the fire, he offers the two Aghara oblations as at the sacrifices of the new and full moon, silently.

2.s: athājyabhāgau juhotyagnaye svāhetyuttarārdhapūrvārdhe somāya svāheti dakṣiṇārdhapūrvārdhe samaṃ pūrveṇa |
2.d: अथाज्यभागौ जुहोत्यग्नये स्वाहेत्युत्तरार्धपूर्वार्धे सोमाय स्वाहेति दक्षिणार्धपूर्वार्धे समं पूर्वेण ।
2.e: Then he offers the two Agyabhaga oblations, over the easterly part of the northerly part (of the fire) with (the words), 'To Agni Svaha!' over the easterly part of the southerly part (another oblation) exactly like the preceding one, with (the words), 'To Soma Svaha!'

2.s: yathopadeśaṃ pradhānāhutīrhutvā jayābhyātānānrāṣṭrabhṛtaḥ prājāpatyāṃ vyāhṛtīrvihṛtāḥ sauviṣṭakṛtīmittyupajuhoti | yadasya karmaṇo 'tyarīricaṃ yadvā nyūnamihākaram | agniṣṭatsviṣṭakṛdvidvāntsarvasviṣṭaṃ suhutaṃ karotu svāheti |
2.d: यथोपदेशं प्रधानाहुतीर्हुत्वा जयाभ्यातानान्राष्ट्रभृतः प्राजापत्यां व्याहृतीर्विहृताः सौविष्टकृतीमित्त्युपजुहोति । यदस्य कर्मणो ऽत्यरीरिचं यद्वा न्यूनमिहाकरम् । अग्निष्टत्स्विष्टकृद्विद्वान्त्सर्वस्विष्टं सुहुतं करोतु स्वाहेति ।
2.e: Having offered the chief oblations (belonging to each sacrifice) according to prescription, he adds the following oblations, viz. the Gaya, Abhyatana, Rashtrabhrit oblations, the oblation to Pragapati, the Vyahritis one by one, the oblation to (Agni) Svishtakrit with (the following formula), 'What I have done too much in this ceremony, or what I have done here too little, all that may Agni Svishtakrit, he who knows, make well sacrificed and well offered. Svaha!'
The sprinkling (of water) round (the fire is repeated) as above; the Mantras are altered so as to say, 'Thou hast given thy consent,' 'Thou hast given thy impulse.'
The designation 'Pakayagna' is used of ceremonies connected with worldly life.
There the ritual based on the Brahmana (holds good),
(To which the words allude), 'He sacrifices twice; he wipes off (his hand) twice; he partakes twice (of the sacrificial food); having gone away he sips (out of the Sruk) and licks off (the Sruk).'

2.s: sarva ṛtavo vivāhasya śaiśirau māsau parihāpyottamaṃ ca naidāgham |
2.d: सर्व ऋतवो विवाहस्य शैशिरौ मासौ परिहाप्योत्तमं च नैदाघम् ।
2.e: All seasons are fit for marriage with the exception of the two months of the sisira season, and of the last summer month.
All Nakshatras which are stated to be pure, (are fit for marriage);
And one should learn from women what ceremonies (are required by custom).
Under the Invakas (Nakshatra), (the wooers who go to the girl's father) are sent out: such wooers are welcome.

3.e: Under the Maghas (Nakshatra) cows are provided;
Under the Phalguni (Nakshatra) marriage is celebrated.

3.s: yāṃ kāmayeta duhitaraṃ priyā syāditi tāṃ niṣṭyāyāṃ dadyāt priyaiva bhavati neva tu punarāgacchatī ti brāhmaṇāvekṣo vidhiḥ |
3.d: यां कामयेत दुहितरं प्रिया स्यादिति तां निष्ट्यायां दद्यात् प्रियैव भवति नेव तु पुनरागच्छती ति ब्राह्मणावेक्षो विधिः ।

3.s: dattāṃ guptāṃ dyotāmṛṣabhāṃ śarabhāṃ vinatāṃ vikaṭāṃ muṇḍāṃ maṇḍūṣikāṃ sāṅkārikāṃ rātāṃ pālīṃ mitrāṃ svanujāṃ varṣakārīṃ ca varjayet |
3.d: दत्तां गुप्तां द्योतामृषभां शरभां विनतां विकटां मुण्डां मण्डूषिकां साङ्कारिकां रातां पालीं मित्रां स्वनुजां वर्षकारीं च वर्जयेत् ।

3.s: nānā bījāni saṃsṛṣṭāni vedyāḥ pāṃsūn kṣetrālloṣṭaṃ śakṛcchmaśānaloṣṭamiti |
3.d: नाना बीजानि संसृष्टानि वेद्याः पांसून् क्षेत्राल्लोष्टं शकृच्छ्मशानलोष्टमिति ।

4.e: Let him send out as his wooers friends who have assembled, who are versed in the Mantras.
He should recite over them the first two verses (Mantrap. I, 1, 1. 2).
When he himself has seen (the bride), let him murmur the third (verse; M. I, 1, 3).
With the fourth (M. I, 1, 4) let him behold her.

4.s: aṅguṣṭhenopamadhyamayā cāṅgulyā darbhaṃ saṃgṛhyottareṇa yajuṣā tasyā bhruvorantaraṃ saṃmṛjya pratīcīnaṃ nirasyet |
4.d: अङ्गुष्ठेनोपमध्यमया चाङ्गुल्या दर्भं संगृह्योत्तरेण यजुषा तस्या भ्रुवोरन्तरं संमृज्य प्रतीचीनं निरस्येत् ।
4.e: Let him seize with his thumb and fourth finger a Darbha blade, and let him wipe (therewith) the interstice between her eye-brows with the next Yagus (M. I, 1, 5), and let him throw it away towards the west.
If an omen occurs (such as the bride's or her relations' weeping), let him murmur the next (verse; M. I, 1, 6).
With the next (verse; M. I, 1, 7) let him send an even number of persons who have assembled there, and who are versed in the Mantras, to fetch water.

4.s: uttareṇa yajuṣā tasyāśśirasi darbheṇvaṃ nidhāya tasminnuttarayā dakṣiṇaṃ yugacchidraṃ pratiṣṭhāpya chidre suvarṇamuttarayāntardhāyottarābhiḥ pañcabhissnāpayitvottarayāhatena vāsasā'cchādyottarayā yoktreṇa sannahyati |
4.d: उत्तरेण यजुषा तस्याश्शिरसि दर्भेण्वं निधाय तस्मिन्नुत्तरया दक्षिणं युगच्छिद्रं प्रतिष्ठाप्य छिद्रे सुवर्णमुत्तरयान्तर्धायोत्तराभिः पञ्चभिस्स्नापयित्वोत्तरयाहतेन वाससाऽच्छाद्योत्तरया योक्त्रेण सन्नह्यति ।
4.e: With the next Yagus (M. I, 1, 8) he places a round piece of Darbha net-work on her head; on that, with the next (verse; M. I, 1, 9) he places a right yoke-hole; on this hole he lays with the next (verse; M. I, 1, 10), a piece of gold, and washes her with the next five verses (M. I, 2, 1-5), (so that the water runs over that gold and through the yoke-hole); with the next (verse; M. I, 2, 6) he causes her to dress in a fresh garment, and with the next (M. I, 2, 7) he girds her with a rope.

4.s: athaināmuttarayā dakṣiṇe haste gṛhītvāgnimabhyānīyāpareṇāgnimudagagraṃ kaṭamāstīrya tasminnupaviśata uttaro varaḥ |
4.d: अथैनामुत्तरया दक्षिणे हस्ते गृहीत्वाग्निमभ्यानीयापरेणाग्निमुदगग्रं कटमास्तीर्य तस्मिन्नुपविशत उत्तरो वरः ।
4.e: Then he takes hold of her with the next (verse; M. I, 2, 8) by her right hand, leads her to the fire, spreads a mat, west of the fire, so that the points of the blades in it are directed towards the north, and on this mat they both sit down, the bridegroom to the north.
After the ceremonies have been performed from the putting of wood on the fire down to the Agyabhaga oblations, he recites over her the first two (verses of the third Anuvaka).

4.s: athāsyai dakṣiṇena nīcā hastena dakṣiṇamuttānaṃ hastaṃ gṛhṇīyāt |
4.d: अथास्यै दक्षिणेन नीचा हस्तेन दक्षिणमुत्तानं हस्तं गृह्णीयात् ।
4.e: Then he should take with his right hand, palm down, her right hand which she holds palm up.
If he wishes that only daughters may be born to him, he should seize only the fingers (without the thumb);

4.s: yadi kāmayeta puṃsa eva janayeyamityaṅguṣṭhameva so 'bhīvāṅguṣṭhamabhīva lomāni gṛhṇāti |
4.d: यदि कामयेत पुंस एव जनयेयमित्यङ्गुष्ठमेव सो ऽभीवाङ्गुष्ठमभीव लोमानि गृह्णाति ।

4.s: athaināmutteraṇāgniṃ dakṣiṇena padā prācīmudīcīṃ vā diśamabhi prakramaya tyekamiṣa iti |
4.d: अथैनामुत्तेरणाग्निं दक्षिणेन पदा प्राचीमुदीचीं वा दिशमभि प्रक्रमय त्येकमिष इति ।

5.s: prāgghomāt pradakṣiṇamagniṃ kṛtvā yathāsthānamupaviśyānvārabdhāyāmuttarā āhutīrjuhoti somāya janivide svāhe tyetaiḥ pratimantram |
5.d: प्राग्घोमात् प्रदक्षिणमग्निं कृत्वा यथास्थानमुपविश्यान्वारब्धायामुत्तरा आहुतीर्जुहोति सोमाय जनिविदे स्वाहे त्येतैः प्रतिमन्त्रम् ।

5.e: He enters upon the performance of the Gaya and following oblations.

5.s: pariṣecanāntaṃ kṛtvottarābhyāṃ yoktraṃ vimucya tāṃ tataḥ pra vā vāhayet pra vā hārayet |
5.d: परिषेचनान्तं कृत्वोत्तराभ्यां योक्त्रं विमुच्य तां ततः प्र वा वाहयेत् प्र वा हारयेत् ।

6.e: The next (verse; M. I, 6, 13), he recites over a boat (with which they are going to cross a river).

6.s: na ca nāvyāṃ staratī vadhūḥ paśyet |
6.d: न च नाव्यां स्तरती वधूः पश्येत् ।
6.e: And let the wife, when she is crossing, not see the crew.
When they have crossed, let him murmur the next (verse; M. I, 6, 14).

6.s: śmaśānādhivyātikrame bhāṇḍe rathe vā riṣṭe 'gnerupasamādhānādyājyabhāgānte 'nvārabdhāyāmuttarā āhutīrhutvā jayādi pratipadyate pariṣecanāntaṃ karoti |
6.d: श्मशानाधिव्यातिक्रमे भाण्डे रथे वा रिष्टे ऽग्नेरुपसमाधानाद्याज्यभागान्ते ऽन्वारब्धायामुत्तरा आहुतीर्हुत्वा जयादि प्रतिपद्यते परिषेचनान्तं करोति ।
6.e: If they have to pass over a cemetery, or if any article (which they carry with them), or their chariot is damaged, the ceremonies from the putting of wood on the fire down to the Agyabhaga oblations are performed, and while she takes hold of him, he offers the oblations (indicated by the) next (Mantras; M. I, 7, 1-7), then he enters upon the performance of the Gaya and following oblations, and performs (the rites) down to the sprinkling (of water) round (the fire).

6.s: kṣīriṇāmanyeṣāṃ vā lakṣmaṇyānāṃ vṛkṣāṇāṃ nadīnāṃ dhanvanāṃ ca vyatikrama uttare yathāliṅgaṃ japet |
6.d: क्षीरिणामन्येषां वा लक्ष्मण्यानां वृक्षाणां नदीनां धन्वनां च व्यतिक्रम उत्तरे यथालिङ्गं जपेत् ।
6.e: If they pass by trees with milky sap or by other trees that serve as marks, by rivers or by deserts, he should murmur the next two (verses; M. I, 7, 8. 9), according to the characteristics in them (which refer to these different cases).
With the next (verse) he shows her the house(M. I, 7, 10).
With the next two (verses; M. I, 7, 11. 12) he unyokes the two animals; the right one first.

6.s: lohitaṃ carmā'naḍuhaṃ prācīnagrīvamuttaraloma madhye 'gārasyottarayā'stīrya gṛhān prapādayannuttarāṃ vācayati dakṣiṇena padā |
6.d: लोहितं चर्माऽनडुहं प्राचीनग्रीवमुत्तरलोम मध्ये ऽगारस्योत्तरयाऽस्तीर्य गृहान् प्रपादयन्नुत्तरां वाचयति दक्षिणेन पदा ।
6.e: Having, with the next (verse; M. I, 8, 1), spread out, in the centre of the house, a red bull's skin with the neck to the east, with the hair up, he causes her to recite the next (verse; M. I, 8, 2), while he makes her enter the house, (which she does) with her right foot.
And she does not stand on the threshold.

6.s: uttarapūrve deśe 'gārasyāgrerupasamādhānādyājyabhāgānte 'nvārabhdhāyāmuttarā āhutīrhutvā jayādi pratipadyate pariṣecanāntaṃ kṛtvottarayā carmaṇyupaviśata uttaro varaḥ |
6.d: उत्तरपूर्वे देशे ऽगारस्याग्रेरुपसमाधानाद्याज्यभागान्ते ऽन्वारभ्धायामुत्तरा आहुतीर्हुत्वा जयादि प्रतिपद्यते परिषेचनान्तं कृत्वोत्तरया चर्मण्युपविशत उत्तरो वरः ।
6.e: In the north-east part of the house the ceremonies from the putting of wood on the fire down to the Agyabhaga oblations are performed, and while she takes hold of him, he offers the oblations (indicated by the) next (Mantras; M. I, 8, 3-15); then he enters upon the performance of the Gaya and following oblations, and performs (the rites) down to the sprinkling (of water) round (the fire). Then they sit down with the next (verse; M. I, 9, 1) on the skin, the bridegroom to the north.

6.s: athāsyāḥ puṃsvorjīvaputrāyāḥ putramaṅka uttarayopaveśya tasmai phalānyuttareṇa yajuṣā pradāyottare japitvā vācaṃ yacchata ā nakṣatrebhyaḥ |
6.d: अथास्याः पुंस्वोर्जीवपुत्रायाः पुत्रमङ्क उत्तरयोपवेश्य तस्मै फलान्युत्तरेण यजुषा प्रदायोत्तरे जपित्वा वाचं यच्छत आ नक्षत्रेभ्यः ।
6.e: He then places with the next (verse; M. I, 9, 2), the son of a wife who has only sons and whose children are alive, in her lap, gives fruits to the (child) with the next Yagus (M. I, 9, 3), and murmurs the next two (verses; M. I, 9, 4-5). Then he (and his wife) observe silence until the stars appear.

6.s: uditeṣu nakṣatreṣu prācīmudīcīṃ vā diśamupaniṣkramyottarābhyāṃ yathāliṅgaṃ dhruvamarundhatīṃ ca darśayati |
6.d: उदितेषु नक्षत्रेषु प्राचीमुदीचीं वा दिशमुपनिष्क्रम्योत्तराभ्यां यथालिङ्गं ध्रुवमरुन्धतीं च दर्शयति ।
6.e: When the stars have appeared, he goes out (of the house with her) in an easterly or northerly direction, and shows her the polar star and (the star) Arundhati with the next two verses (M. I, 9, 6-7), according to the characteristics (contained in those verses).

7.e: He then makes her offer the sacrifice of a Sthalipaka sacred to Agni.
The wife husks (the rice grains out of which this Sthalipaka is prepared).

After he has cooked (the Sthalipaka), and has sprinkled (Agya) over it, and has taken it from the fire towards the east or the north, and has sprinkled (Agya) over it while it stands (there near the fire), (the ceremonies) from the putting of wood on the fire down to the Agyabhaga oblations (are performed), and while she takes hold of him, he sacrifices of that Sthalipaka.
The 'spreading under' and the sprinkling over (of Agya are done) once; two Avadanas (or cut-off portions are taken).
Agni is the deity (of the first oblation); the offering is made with the word Svaha.
Or he may sacrifice after having picked out, once, a portion (of the sacrificial food with the Darvi spoon).
Agni Svishtakrit is the second (deity).
(At the Svishtakrit oblation) the 'spreading under' and taking an Avadana are done once, the sprinkling over (of Agya) twice.
The Avadana for the first deity (is taken) out of the middle (of the Sthalipaka);
It is offered over the centre (of the fire).
(The Avadana) for the second (deity is taken) from the northern part (of the Sthalipaka);
It is offered over the easterly part of the northerly part (of the fire).

7.s: lepayoḥ prastaravat tūṣṇīṃ barhi raṅtvā gnau praharati |
7.d: लेपयोः प्रस्तरवत् तूष्णीं बर्हि रङ्त्वा ग्नौ प्रहरति ।
7.e: Having silently anointed (a part of) the Barhis (by dipping it) into the remains both (of the Sthalipaka and the Agya) in the way prescribed (in the Srauta ritual) for the (part of the Barhis called) Prastara, he throws (that part of the Barhis) into the fire.
(The rule regarding) the second sprinkling (of water round the fire) is valid (here).
He gives (the remains of) that (sacrificial food) with butter to a Brahmana to eat--
Whom he reveres. To that (Brahmana) he makes the present of a bull.
In the same way, with the exception of the sacrificial gift, they should sacrifice a Sthalipaka from then onwards, on the days of the new and full moon, after having fasted.
Some say that a vessel full (of grain) is the sacrificial gift.

7.s: sāyaṃ prātarata ūrdhva hastenaite āhutī taṇḍulairyavairvā juhuyāt |
7.d: सायं प्रातरत ऊर्ध्व हस्तेनैते आहुती तण्डुलैर्यवैर्वा जुहुयात् ।
7.e: From then onwards he should offer morning and evening with his hand these two oblations (to Agni and to Agni Svishtakrit) of (rice) grains or of barley.
The deities are the same as at the Sthalipaka (just described).
Some say that the first oblation in the morning is sacred to Surya.
Before and after (those oblations) the sprinkling (of water) round (the fire is performed) as stated above.
By the sacrifice of the new and full moon the other ceremonies have been explained (the knowledge of) which is derived from practice.

8.e: At the opening and concluding ceremonies of the Vedic study, the Rishi who is indicated (as the [paragraph continues] Rishi of the Kanda which they study, is the deity to whom the ceremony belongs),
And in the second place Sadasaspati (cf. Mantrap. I, 9, 8).

They reject a sacrifice performed by a wife or by one who has not received the Upanayana initiation, and a sacrifice of salt or pungent food, or of such food as has an admixture of a despised sort of food.
Sacrifices connected with special wishes and Bali sacrifices (should be performed) as stated (even against the clauses of the last Sutra).
Whenever the fire flames up of itself, he should put two pieces of wood on it with the next two (verses: M. I, 9, 9-10),
Or with (the two formulas), 'May fortune reach me! May fortune come to me!'
Let him notice the day on which he brings his wife home.
(From that day) through three nights they should both sleep on the ground, they should be chaste, and should avoid salt and pungent food.

8.s: tayośśayyāmanteraṇa daṇḍo gandhalipto vāsasā sūtreṇa vā parivītastiṣṭhati |
8.d: तयोश्शय्यामन्तेरण दण्डो गन्धलिप्तो वाससा सूत्रेण वा परिवीतस्तिष्ठति ।
8.e: Between their sleeping-places a staff is interposed, which is anointed with perfumes and wrapped round with a garment or a thread.

8.s: taṃ caturthyāpararātra uttarābhyāmutthāpya prakṣālya nidhāyāgnerupasamādhānādyājyabhāgānte 'nvārabdhāyāmuttarā āhutīrhutvā jayādi pratipadyate pariṣecanāntaṃ kṛtvāpareṇāgniṃ prācīmupaveśya tasyāśśirasyājyaśeṣādvyāhṛtibhiroṅkāracaturthābhirānīyottarābhyāṃ yathāliṅgaṃ mithassamīkṣyottarayā'jyaśeṣeṇa hṛdayadeśai saṃmṛjyottarāstisro japitvā śeṣaṃ samāveśane japet |
8.d: तं चतुर्थ्यापररात्र उत्तराभ्यामुत्थाप्य प्रक्षाल्य निधायाग्नेरुपसमाधानाद्याज्यभागान्ते ऽन्वारब्धायामुत्तरा आहुतीर्हुत्वा जयादि प्रतिपद्यते परिषेचनान्तं कृत्वापरेणाग्निं प्राचीमुपवेश्य तस्याश्शिरस्याज्यशेषाद्व्याहृतिभिरोङ्कारचतुर्थाभिरानीयोत्तराभ्यां यथालिङ्गं मिथस्समीक्ष्योत्तरयाऽज्यशेषेण हृदयदेशै संमृज्योत्तरास्तिस्रो जपित्वा शेषं समावेशने जपेत् ।
8.e: In the last part of the fourth night he takes up the (staff) with the next two (verses; M. I, 10, 1-2), washes it and put it away; then (the ceremonies) from the putting of wood on the fire down to the Agyabhaga oblations (are performed), and while she takes hold of him, he sacrifices the oblations (indicated by the) next (Mantras; M. I, 10, 3-9); then he enters upon the performance of the Gaya and following oblations, and performs (the rites) down to the sprinkling (of water) round (the fire). Then he makes her sit down to the west of the fire, facing the east, and pours some Agya of the remains (of those oblations) on her head with the (three) Vyahritis and the word Om as the fourth (M. I, 10, 10-13). Then they look at each other with the next two verses (M. I, 11, 1-2), according to the characteristics (contained in those verses); with the next verse (M. I, 11, 3) he besmears the region of their hearts with remains of Agya; then he should murmur the next three verses (I, 11, 4-6), and should murmur the rest (of the Anuvaka; I, 11, 7-11) when cohabiting with her.
Or another person should recite (the rest of the Anuvaka) over her, (before they cohabit).

8.s: yadā malavadvāsāḥ syādathaināṃ brāhmaṇapratiṣiddhāni karmāṇi saṃśāsti 'yāṃ malavadvāsasa' mityetāni |
8.d: यदा मलवद्वासाः स्यादथैनां ब्राह्मणप्रतिषिद्धानि कर्माणि संशास्ति ऽयां मलवद्वाससऽ मित्येतानि ।
8.e: During her (first) monthly illness he instructs her about the things forbidden (to menstruous women), contained in the Brahmana, in the section, 'A menstruous woman with whom,' &c.
After the appearance of her monthly illness, he should, when going to cohabit with her after her illness, recite over her, after she has bathed, the next verses (M. I, 12, 1-13, 4).

9.e: Each following night with an even number, from the fourth (after the beginning of her monthly illness) till the sixteenth, brings more excellent offspring to them, if chosen for the (first) cohabiting after her illness; thus it is said.

9.s: arthaprādhvasya parikṣave parikāsane cāpa upaspṛśyottare yathāliṅgaṃ japet |
9.d: अर्थप्राध्वस्य परिक्षवे परिकासने चाप उपस्पृश्योत्तरे यथालिङ्गं जपेत् ।
9.e: If he sneezes or coughs while going about on business, he should touch water and should murmur the two following (verses; M. I, 13, 5. 6) according to the characteristics (which they contain).

9.s: evamuttarairyathāliṅgaṃ citriyaṃ vanaspatiṃ śakṛdrīti sigvātaṃ śakunimiti |
9.d: एवमुत्तरैर्यथालिङ्गं चित्रियं वनस्पतिं शकृद्रीति सिग्वातं शकुनिमिति ।
9.e: In the same way with the next (Mantras--M. I, 13, 7-10--he should address the following objects), according to the characteristics (which those Mantras contain): a conspicuous tree, a heap of excrements, the skirt (of his garment) which is blown against him by the wind, and a shrieking bird.

9.s: ubhayorhṛdayasaṃsarge 'psustrirātrāvaraṃ brahmacarya caritvā sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvāgnerupasamādhānādyājyabhāgānte 'nvārabdhāyāṃ sthālīpākāduttarā āhutīrhutvā jayādi pratipadyate pariṣecanāntaṃ kṛtvā tena sarpiṣmatā yugmān dvyavarān brāhmaṇān bhojayitvā sidviṃ vācayīta |
9.d: उभयोर्हृदयसंसर्गे ऽप्सुस्त्रिरात्रावरं ब्रह्मचर्य चरित्वा स्थालीपाकं श्रपयित्वाग्नेरुपसमाधानाद्याज्यभागान्ते ऽन्वारब्धायां स्थालीपाकादुत्तरा आहुतीर्हुत्वा जयादि प्रतिपद्यते परिषेचनान्तं कृत्वा तेन सर्पिष्मता युग्मान् द्व्यवरान् ब्राह्मणान् भोजयित्वा सिद्विं वाचयीत ।
9.e: One (for instance, the wife's father) who wishes that the hearts of both (husband and wife) may be in accord should observe chastity through at least three nights and should prepare a Sthalipaka. Then (the ceremonies) from the putting (of wood) on (the fire) down to the Agyabhaga oblations (are performed), and while the wife takes hold of him, he sacrifices of the Sthalipaka the oblations (indicated by the) next (Mantras; M. I, 14, 1-7); then he enters upon the performance of the Gaya and following oblations, and performs (the rites) down to the sprinkling (of water) round (the fire). (The remains of) the (sacrificial food) with butter, he should give to eat to an even number of Brahmanas, at least to two, and should cause them to pronounce wishes for his success.

9.s: śvastiṣyeṇeti trissaptairyavaiḥ pāṭhāṃ parikirati"yadi vāruṇyasi varuṇāttvā niṣkrīṇāmi yadi saumyasi somāttvā niṣkrīṇāmi"iti |
9.d: श्वस्तिष्येणेति त्रिस्सप्तैर्यवैः पाठां परिकिरति"यदि वारुण्यसि वरुणात्त्वा निष्क्रीणामि यदि सौम्यसि सोमात्त्वा निष्क्रीणामि"इति ।
9.e: When the moon, on the following day, will be in conjunction with Tishya, she strews three times seven barley-grains around (the plant) Clypea Hernandifolia with (the formula), 'If thou belongest to Varuna, I redeem thee from Varuna. If thou belongest to Soma, I redeem thee from Soma.'

9.s: śvobhūte uttarayotthāpyottarābhistisṛbhirabhimantryottarayā praticchannāṃ hastayorābadhya śayyākāle bāhubhyāṃ bhartāraṃ parigṛhṇīyādupadhānaliṅgayā |
9.d: श्वोभूते उत्तरयोत्थाप्योत्तराभिस्तिसृभिरभिमन्त्र्योत्तरया प्रतिच्छन्नां हस्तयोराबध्य शय्याकाले बाहुभ्यां भर्तारं परिगृह्णीयादुपधानलिङ्गया ।
9.e: On the following day she should set upright (the plant) with the next (verse; M. I, 15, 1), should recite the next three (verses; M. I, 15, 2-4) over it, should tie (its root) with the next (verse; M. I, 15, 5) to her hands so that (her husband) does not see it, and should, when they have gone to bed, embrace her husband with her arms, with the verse alluding to the word upadhana ('putting on;' M. I, 15, 6).
Thus he will be subject to her.
By this (rite) also (a wife) overcomes her co-wives.
For this same purpose she worships the sun daily with the next Anuvaka (M. I, 16).

9.s: yakṣmagṛhītāmanyāṃ vā brahmacaryayuktaḥ puṣkarasaṃvartamūlairuttarairyathāliṅgamaṅgāni saṃmṛśya pratīcīnaṃ nirasyet |
9.d: यक्ष्मगृहीतामन्यां वा ब्रह्मचर्ययुक्तः पुष्करसंवर्तमूलैरुत्तरैर्यथालिङ्गमङ्गानि संमृश्य प्रतीचीनं निरस्येत् ।
9.e: If a wife is affected with consumption or is otherwise sick, one who has to observe chastity, should rub her limbs with young lotus leaves which are still rolled up, and with lotus roots, with the next (formulas, limb by limb) according to the characteristics (contained in those formulas; M. I, 17, 1-6), and should throw away (the leaves and roots) towards the west.
With the next (verses; M. I, 17, 7-10) he should give the wife's garment (which she has worn at the wedding [?]) to (a Brahmana) who knows this (ceremony).

10.e: We shall explain the Upanayana (or initiation of the student).
Let him initiate a Brahmana in the eighth year after the conception,
A Raganya in the eleventh, a Vaisya in the twelfth year after the conception.
Spring, summer, autumn: these are the (fit) seasons (for the Upanayana), corresponding to the order of the castes.

10.s: brāhmaṇānbhojayitvā'śiṣo vācayitvā kumāraṃ bhojayitvānuvākasya prathamena yajuṣāpaḥ saṃsṛjyoṣṇāśśītāsvānīyottarayā śira unatti |
10.d: ब्राह्मणान्भोजयित्वाऽशिषो वाचयित्वा कुमारं भोजयित्वानुवाकस्य प्रथमेन यजुषापः संसृज्योष्णाश्शीतास्वानीयोत्तरया शिर उनत्ति ।
10.e: (The boy's father) serves food to Brahmanas and causes them to pronounce auspicious wishes, and serves food to the boy. (The teacher?) pours together, with the first Yagus (of the next Anuvaka, warm and cold) water, pouring the warm water into the cold, and moistens (the boy's) head with the next (verse; M. II, 1, 2).

Having put three Darbha blades into his hair (towards each of the four directions) (the teacher [?]) shaves his hair with the next four (verses; M. II, 1, 3-6) with the different Mantras, towards the different (four) directions.
With the following (verse, M. II, 1, 7, somebody) addresses him while he is shaving.

10.s: ānaḍuhe śakṛtpiṇḍe yavānnidhāya tasmin keśānupayamyottarayodumbaramūle darbhastambe vā nidadhāti |
10.d: आनडुहे शकृत्पिण्डे यवान्निधाय तस्मिन् केशानुपयम्योत्तरयोदुम्बरमूले दर्भस्तम्बे वा निदधाति ।
10.e: Towards the south, his mother or a Brahmakarin strews barley-grains on a lump of bull's dung; with this (dung) she catches up the hair (that is cut off), and puts it down with the next (verse; M. II, 1, 8) at the root of an Udumbara tree or in a tuft of Darbha grass.

After (the boy) has bathed, and (the ceremonies) from the putting (of wood) on (the fire) down to the Agyabhaga oblations (have been performed), he causes him to put a piece of Palasa wood on the fire with the next (verse; M. II, 2, 1), and makes him tread with his right foot on a stone to the north of the fire, with (the verse), 'Tread' (M. II, 2, 2).

Having recited the next two (verses; M. II. 2, 3. 4) over a garment that has been spun and woven on one day, and has caused him, with the next three (verses; M. II. 2, 5-7), to put it on, he recites over him, after he has put it on, the next (verse; M. II, 2, 8).

10.s: mauñjīṃ mekhalāṃ trivṛtāṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇamuttarābhyāṃ parivīyājinamuttaramuttarayā |
10.d: मौञ्जीं मेखलां त्रिवृतां त्रिः प्रदक्षिणमुत्तराभ्यां परिवीयाजिनमुत्तरमुत्तरया ।
10.e: He ties thrice around him, from left to right, a threefold-twisted girdle of Munga grass with the next two (verses; M. II. 2, 9. 10), and (gives him) a skin as his outer garment with the next (verse; II, 2, 11).

10.s: uttareṇāgniṃ darbhān saṃstīrya teṣvenamuttarayāvasthāpyodakāñjalimasmā añjalāvānīyottarayā triḥ prokṣyottarairdakṣiṇe haste gṛhītvottarairdevatābhyaḥ parīdāyottareṇa yajuṣopanīya 'suprajā'iti dakṣiṇe karṇe japati |
10.d: उत्तरेणाग्निं दर्भान् संस्तीर्य तेष्वेनमुत्तरयावस्थाप्योदकाञ्जलिमस्मा अञ्जलावानीयोत्तरया त्रिः प्रोक्ष्योत्तरैर्दक्षिणे हस्ते गृहीत्वोत्तरैर्देवताभ्यः परीदायोत्तरेण यजुषोपनीय ऽसुप्रजाऽइति दक्षिणे कर्णे जपति ।
10.e: To the north of the fire (the teacher) spreads out Darbha grass; on that he causes (the boy) to station himself with the next (verse; M. II. 3, 1), pours his joined hands full of water into (the boy's) joined hands, makes him sprinkle himself three times with the next (verse; M. II, 3, 2), takes hold of his right hand with the next (formulas; M. II, 3, 3-12), gives him with the next (formulas; M. II, 3, 13-23) in charge to the deities (mentioned in those Mantras), initiates him with the next Yagus (M. II, 3, 24), and murmurs into his right ear the (Mantra), 'Blessed with offspring' (II, 3, 25).

11.e: The boy says, 'I am come to be a student' (II, 3, 26).
The other (i.e. the teacher) has to ask; the boy has to answer (II, 3, 27-30).
The other murmurs the rest (of the Anuvaka),
And causes the boy to repeat (the Mantra) which contains wishes for himself (II, 3, 32).
(The rites) down to the Agyabhagas have been prescribed.
Having then caused him to sacrifice the oblations (indicated in the) next (Mantras; M. II, 4, 1-11), he enters upon (the performance) of the Gaya and following oblations.

11.s: pariṣecanāntaṃ kṛtvāpareṇāgnimudagagraṃ kūrca nidhāya tasminnuttareṇa yajuṣopanetopaviśati |
11.d: परिषेचनान्तं कृत्वापरेणाग्निमुदगग्रं कूर्च निधाय तस्मिन्नुत्तरेण यजुषोपनेतोपविशति ।
11.e: Having performed (the rites) down to the sprinkling (of water) round (the fire), he puts down, to the west of the fire, a bunch of northward-pointed grass; on that (the teacher) who performs the initiation, sits down with the next Yagus (M. II, 4, 12).

11.s: purastāt pratyaṅṅāsīnaḥ kumāro dakṣiṇena pāṇinā dakṣiṇaṃ pādamanvārabhyāha 'sāvitrīṃ bho anubrūhi'iti |
11.d: पुरस्तात् प्रत्यङ्ङासीनः कुमारो दक्षिणेन पाणिना दक्षिणं पादमन्वारभ्याह ऽसावित्रीं भो अनुब्रूहिऽइति ।

11.s: pālāśo daṇḍo brāhmaṇasya naiyyagrodhasskandhajo 'vāṅgro rājanyasya bādara audumbaro vā vaiśyasya |
11.d: पालाशो दण्डो ब्राह्मणस्य नैय्यग्रोधस्स्कन्धजो ऽवाङ्ग्रो राजन्यस्य बादर औदुम्बरो वा वैश्यस्य ।

11.s: smṛtaṃ ca ma ityetadvācayitvā gurave varaṃ datvodāyuṣetyutthāpyottarairādityamupatiṣṭhate |
11.d: स्मृतं च म इत्येतद्वाचयित्वा गुरवे वरं दत्वोदायुषेत्युत्थाप्योत्तरैरादित्यमुपतिष्ठते ।

11.s: yaṃ kāmayeta nāyama cchidyeteti tamuttarayā dakṣiṇe haste gṛhṇīyāt |
11.d: यं कामयेत नायम च्छिद्येतेति तमुत्तरया दक्षिणे हस्ते गृह्णीयात् ।

11.s: pari tve ti parimṛjya tasminnuttarairmantraissamidha ādadhyāt |
11.d: परि त्वे ति परिमृज्य तस्मिन्नुत्तरैर्मन्त्रैस्समिध आदध्यात् ।

12.s: vedamadhītya snāsyan pragudayādvrajaṃ praviśyāntarlomnā carmaṇā dvāramaparidhāyā'ste |
12.d: वेदमधीत्य स्नास्यन् प्रगुदयाद्व्रजं प्रविश्यान्तर्लोम्ना चर्मणा द्वारमपरिधायाऽस्ते ।
12.e: Having studied the Veda, when going to take the bath (which signifies the end of his studentship), he enters a cow-shed before sunrise, hangs over its door a skin with the hair inside, and sits there.
On that day the sun should not shine upon him.

12.s: madhyandine 'gnerupasamādhānādyājyabhāgānte pālāśīṃ samidhamuttarayā'dhāyāpareṇāgniṃ kaṭa erakāyāṃ vopaviśyottarayā kṣuramabhimantryottareṇa yajuṣā vaptre pradāyāpāṃ saṃsarjanādyākeśanidhānāt samānam |
12.d: मध्यन्दिने ऽग्नेरुपसमाधानाद्याज्यभागान्ते पालाशीं समिधमुत्तरयाऽधायापरेणाग्निं कट एरकायां वोपविश्योत्तरया क्षुरमभिमन्त्र्योत्तरेण यजुषा वप्त्रे प्रदायापां संसर्जनाद्याकेशनिधानात् समानम् ।
12.e: At noon, after (the ceremonies) from the putting (of wood) on the fire down to the Agyabhaga oblations (have been performed), he puts a piece of Palasa wood on (the fire) with the next (verse; M. II, 7, 1), sits down to the west of the fire on a mat or on eraka grass, recites the next (verse, II, 7, 2) over a razor, and hands it over to the barber with the next Yagus (II, 7, 3). (The rites) beginning with the pouring together of (warm and cold) water down to the burying of the hair are the same as above (comp. M. II, 7, 4).

12.s: jaghanārdhe vrajasyopaviśya vistrasya mekhalāṃ brahmacāriṇe prayacchati |
12.d: जघनार्धे व्रजस्योपविश्य विस्त्रस्य मेखलां ब्रह्मचारिणे प्रयच्छति ।
12.e: He sits down behind the cow-shed, takes the girdle off, and hands it over to a Brahmakarin.

12.s: tāṃ sa uttareṇa yajuṣodumbaramūle darbhastambe vopagūhati |
12.d: तां स उत्तरेण यजुषोदुम्बरमूले दर्भस्तम्बे वोपगूहति ।
12.e: The (Brahmakarin) hides it with the next Yagus (II, 7, 5) at the root of an Udumbara tree or in a tuft of Darbha grass.
With water of the description stated above he bathes with the six next (verses; II, 7, 6-11), and with the next (II, 7, 12) he cleanses his teeth with a stick of Udumbara wood.
Having bathed and shampooed his body with such ingredients as are used in bathing, (aromatic powder, &c.),

12.s: uttareṇa yajuṣāhatamantaraṃ vāsaḥ paridhāya sārvasurabhiṇā candanenottarairdevatābhyaḥ pradāyottarayānulipya maṇiṃ sauvarṇaṃ sopadhānaṃ sūtrotamuttarayodapātre triḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ pariplāvyottarayā grīvasvābadhyaivameva bādaraṃ maṇiṃ mantravarja savye pāṇāvābadhyāhatamuttaraṃ vāso 'revatīstveti'samānam |
12.d: उत्तरेण यजुषाहतमन्तरं वासः परिधाय सार्वसुरभिणा चन्दनेनोत्तरैर्देवताभ्यः प्रदायोत्तरयानुलिप्य मणिं सौवर्णं सोपधानं सूत्रोतमुत्तरयोदपात्रे त्रिः प्रदक्षिणं परिप्लाव्योत्तरया ग्रीवस्वाबध्यैवमेव बादरं मणिं मन्त्रवर्ज सव्ये पाणावाबध्याहतमुत्तरं वासो ऽरेवतीस्त्वेतिऽसमानम् ।
12.e: He puts on with the next Yagus (M. II, 7, 13) a fresh under garment, and anoints himself, after having given the salve in charge of the deities with the next (Mantras, II, 7, 14), with the next (verse, II, 7, 15) with sandal salve which is scented with all kinds of perfumes. With the next (verse, II, 7, 16) he moves about a gold pellet with its setting, which is strung on a string, three times from left to right in a water-pot; with the next (verse, II, 7, 17) he ties the (pellet) to his neck; in the same way, without Mantras, he ties a pellet of Badara wood to his left hand, and repeats the rites stated above with a fresh upper garment, with the (verses), 'May the rich' (comp. above, IV, 10, 10; M. II, 7, 18).

12.s: tasya daśāyāṃ pravṛrtau prabadhya darvyāmādhāyājyenābhyānāyannuttarā āhutīrhutvā jayādi pratipadyate |
12.d: तस्य दशायां प्रवृर्तौ प्रबध्य दर्व्यामाधायाज्येनाभ्यानायन्नुत्तरा आहुतीर्हुत्वा जयादि प्रतिपद्यते ।
12.e: To the skirt (of that garment) he ties two earrings, puts them into the (sacrificial spoon called) Darvi, offers the oblations (indicated by the) next (Mantras; M. II, 8, 1-8), pouring the Agya over (the ear-rings), and enters upon (the performance of) the Gaya and following oblations.

Having performed (the ceremonies) down to the sprinkling (of water) round (the fire), he should tie (one of the ear-rings) with the same (verses) to his right ear, and with the same (verses one) to his left ear.

In the same way he should with the following (formulas, M. II, 8, 9-9, 5), according to the characteristics (contained in them), (put) a wreath on his head, anoint (his eyes), look into a mirror, (put on) shoes, (and should take) a parasol and a staff.
He keeps silence until the stars appear.

12.s: uditeṣu nakṣatreṣu prācīmudīcīṃ vā diśamupaniṣkramyottareṇārrdhacena diśa upasthāyottareṇa nakṣatrāṇi candramasamiti |
12.d: उदितेषु नक्षत्रेषु प्राचीमुदीचीं वा दिशमुपनिष्क्रम्योत्तरेणार्र्धचेन दिश उपस्थायोत्तरेण नक्षत्राणि चन्द्रमसमिति ।
12.e: When the stars have appeared, he goes away towards the east or north, worships the quarters (of the horizon) with the next hemistich, and the stars and the moon with the next (M. II, 9, 6).
Having spoken with a friend he may go where he likes.

13.s: athaitadaparaṃ tūṣṇīmeva tīrthe snātvā tūṣṇī samidhamādadhāti |
13.d: अथैतदपरं तूष्णीमेव तीर्थे स्नात्वा तूष्णी समिधमादधाति ।
13.e: Now this (is) another (way for performing the Samavartana). He bathes silently at a bathing-place and puts silently a piece of wood on (the fire).

13.s: yatrāsmā apacitiṃ kurvanti tatkūrca upaviśati yathāpurastāt |
13.d: यत्रास्मा अपचितिं कुर्वन्ति तत्कूर्च उपविशति यथापुरस्तात् ।
13.e: He sits down on a bunch of grass, as stated above (comp. M. II, 9, 7), at a place where they are going to honour him (with the Argha reception).
A king and a chieftain (sit down) in the same way (as a Brahmana), with the next two (formulas, M. II, 9, 8. 9), according to the characteristics (contained in them).
(The host) announces (to the guest), 'The water for washing the feet!'

13.s: uttarayābhimantrya dakṣiṇaṃ pādaṃ brāhmaṇāya prayacchetsavyaṃ śūdrāya |
13.d: उत्तरयाभिमन्त्र्य दक्षिणं पादं ब्राह्मणाय प्रयच्छेत्सव्यं शूद्राय ।
13.e: (The guest) should recite the next (verse, II, 9, 10) over (that water) and should stretch out the right foot first to a Brahmana, the left to a Sudra.
Having touched the person who washes him, he should touch himself (i.e. his own heart) with the next (formula, M. II, 9, II).

13.d: कूर्चाभ्यां परिगृह्य मृन्मयेनार् ऽहणीया आप ऽइति प्राह ।
13.e: (The host, taking the Argha water) in an earthen vessel which he holds with two bunches of grass, announces (to the guest), 'The Argha water!'
(The guest) should recite the next (formula, II, 9, 12) over (that water) and should murmur the next Yagus (II, 9, 13), while a part (of the water) is poured over his joined hands.
Over the rest (of the water) which is poured out towards the east, he recites the next (verse, M. II, 9, 14).

13.s: dadhi madhviti saṃsṛjya kāṃsyena varṣīyasā pidhāya kūrcābhyāṃ parigṛhya 'madhuparka 'iti prāha |
13.d: दधि मध्विति संसृज्य कांस्येन वर्षीयसा पिधाय कूर्चाभ्यां परिगृह्य ऽमधुपर्क ऽइति प्राह ।
13.e: (The host) pours together curds and honey in a brass vessel, covers it with a larger (brass cover), takes hold of it with two bunches of grass, and announces (to the guest), 'The honey-mixture!'
Some take three substances, (those stated before) and ghee.
Some take five, (the three stated before), and grains, and flour.

13.s: uttarābhyāmabhintrya yajurbhyāmapa ācāmati purastādupariṣṭāccottarayā triḥ prāśyānukampyāya prayacchet |
13.d: उत्तराभ्यामभिन्त्र्य यजुर्भ्यामप आचामति पुरस्तादुपरिष्टाच्चोत्तरया त्रिः प्राश्यानुकम्प्याय प्रयच्छेत् ।
13.e: The guest recites the next two (formulas, M. II, 10, 1. 2) over (the honey-mixture) and sips water with the two Yagus (II, 10, 3. 4) before (eating) and afterwards; with the next (verse, II, 10, 5) he should partake three times (of the food) and should give the remainder to a person towards whom he is kindly disposed.
A king or a chieftain should only accept it and (give it) to his Purohita.
(The host) announces the cow with (the word), 'The cow!'

13.s: uttarayābhimantrya tasyai vapāṃ śrapayitvopastīrṇābhighāritāṃ madhyamenāntamena vā palāśaparṇenottarayā juhoti |
13.d: उत्तरयाभिमन्त्र्य तस्यै वपां श्रपयित्वोपस्तीर्णाभिघारितां मध्यमेनान्तमेन वा पलाशपर्णेनोत्तरया जुहोति ।
13.e: After the guest has recited the next (formula, M. II, 10, 6) over (the cow, the host) cools its omentum, and having performed the 'spreading under' and the sprinkling over (of Agya), he sacrifices it with the next (verse, M. II, 10, 7) with a Palasa leaf from the middle or the end (of the stalk).
If the guest chooses to let (the cow) loose, he murmurs the next (formulas, II, 10, 8-11) in a low voice (and says) loudly, 'Om! Let it loose!' (II, 10, 12).
(In this case) he recites the next (formulas, M. II, 10, 13-17) in a low voice over the food which is announced to him (instead of the cow), (and says) loudly, 'Om! Make it ready!' (II, 10, 18).

13.s: ācāryāyartvije śvaśurāya rājña iti parisaṃvatsarādupatiṣṭhadbhya etatkāryam |
13.d: आचार्यायर्त्विजे श्वशुराय राज्ञ इति परिसंवत्सरादुपतिष्ठद्भ्य एतत्कार्यम् ।
13.e: For his teacher, for a Ritvig, for his father-in-law, for a king he ought to perform this (Arghya ceremony) as often as they visit his house, if at least one year has elapsed (since they came last).
For a renowned teacher (of the Veda the ceremony should be performed) once.

14.e: The Simantonnayana (or parting of the pregnant wife's hair, is performed) in her first pregnancy, in the fourth month.

14.d: ब्राह्मणान्भोजयित्वाऽशिषो वाचयित्वाग्नेरुपसमाधानाद्याज्यभागान्ते ऽन्वारब्धायामुत्तरा आहुतीर्हुत्वा जयादि प्रतिपद्यते ।
14.e: (The husband) serves food to Brahmanas and causes them to pronounce auspicious wishes; then, after (the ceremonies) from the putting (of wood) on the fire down to the Agyabhaga oblations (have been performed), he offers the oblations (indicated in the) next (Mantras, M. II, 11, 1-8), while (the wife) takes hold of him, and enters upon the (performance) of the Gaya and following oblations.

14.s: pariṣecanāntaṃ kṛtvāpareṇāgniṃ prācīmupaveśya treṇyā śalalyā tribhirdarbhapuñjīlaiśśalāluglapsenetyūrdhva sīmantamunnayati vyāhṛtībhiruttarābhyāṃ ca |
14.d: परिषेचनान्तं कृत्वापरेणाग्निं प्राचीमुपवेश्य त्रेण्या शलल्या त्रिभिर्दर्भपुञ्जीलैश्शलालुग्लप्सेनेत्यूर्ध्व सीमन्तमुन्नयति व्याहृतीभिरुत्तराभ्यां च ।
14.e: Having performed (the rites) down to the sprinkling (of water) round (the fire), he makes her sit down to the west of the fire, facing the east, and parts her hair upwards (i.e. beginning from the front) with a porcupine's quill that has three white spots, with three Darbha blades, and with a bunch of unripe Udumbara fruits, with the Vyahritis or with the two next (verses, II, 11, 9. 10).
Of the next two (verses, II, 11, 11. 12) the first (is to be sung on this occasion) among the (people of the) Salvas.
The second (is to be used) for Brahmanas; and the river near which they dwell is to be named.
He ties barley-grains with young shoots (to the head of the wife); then she keeps silence until the stars appear.

14.s: uduteṣu nakṣatreṣu prācīmudīcīṃ vā diśamupaniṣkramya vatsamanvārabhya vyāhṛtīśca japitvā vācaṃ visṛjet |
14.d: उदुतेषु नक्षत्रेषु प्राचीमुदीचीं वा दिशमुपनिष्क्रम्य वत्समन्वारभ्य व्याहृतीश्च जपित्वा वाचं विसृजेत् ।
14.e: When the stars have appeared, he goes (with his wife) towards the east or north, touches a calf, and murmurs the Vyahritis; then she breaks her silence.
The Pumsavana (i.e. the ceremony to secure the birth of a male child) is performed when the pregnancy has become visible, under the constellation Tishya.

14.s: nyagrodhasya yā prācyudīcīṃ vā śākhā tatassavṛṣaṇāṃ śuṅgāmāhṛtya sīmantavadagnerupasamādhānādi |
14.d: न्यग्रोधस्य या प्राच्युदीचीं वा शाखा ततस्सवृषणां शुङ्गामाहृत्य सीमन्तवदग्नेरुपसमाधानादि ।
14.e: From a branch of a Nyagrodha tree, which points eastward or northward, he takes a shoot with two (fruits that look like) testicles. The putting (of wood) on the fire, &c., is performed as at the Simantonnayana (Sutra 2).

14.s: anavasnātayā kumāryā dṛṣatputre dṛṣatputreṇa peṣayitvā pariplāvyāperaṇāgniṃ prācīmuttānāṃ nipātyottareṇa yajuṣāṅguṣṭhena dakṣiṇe nāsikācchidre 'pinayati |
14.d: अनवस्नातया कुमार्या दृषत्पुत्रे दृषत्पुत्रेण पेषयित्वा परिप्लाव्यापेरणाग्निं प्राचीमुत्तानां निपात्योत्तरेण यजुषाङ्गुष्ठेन दक्षिणे नासिकाच्छिद्रे ऽपिनयति ।
14.e: He causes a girl who has not yet attained maturity to pound (the Nyagrodha shoot) on an upper mill-stone with another upper mill-stone, and to pour water on it; then he makes his wife lie down on her back to the west of the fire, facing the east, and inserts (the pounded substance) with his thumb into her right nostril, with the next Yagus (II, 11, 13).
Then she will give birth to a son.
Here follows the ceremony to secure a quick deliverance.

14.d: अनाप्रीतेन शरावेणानुस्रोतसमुदकमाहृत्य पत्तस्तूर्यन्तीं निधाय मूर्धञ्छोष्यन्तीमुत्तरेण यजुषाभिमृश्यैताभिरद्भिरुत्तराभिरवोक्षेत् ।
14.e: With a shallow cup that has not been used before, he draws water in the direction of the river's current; at his wifeśfeet he lays down a Turyanti plant; he should then touch his wife, who is soon to be delivered, on the head, with the next Yagus (II, 11, 14), and should sprinkle her with the water, with the next (three) verses (II, 11, 15-17).
Yadi garayu na pated evamvihitabhir evadbhir uttarabhyam (II, 11, 18. 19) avokshet.

15.s: jātaṃ vātsapreṇābhimṛśyottareṇa yajuṣopastha ādhāyottarābhyamābhimantraṇaṃ mūrdhanyavaghrāṇaṃ dakṣiṇe karṇe jāpaḥ |
15.d: जातं वात्सप्रेणाभिमृश्योत्तरेण यजुषोपस्थ आधायोत्तराभ्यमाभिमन्त्रणं मूर्धन्यवघ्राणं दक्षिणे कर्णे जापः ।
15.e: After he has touched the new-born child with the Vatsapra hymn (Taitt. Samh. IV, 2, 2; M. II, 11, 20), and has taken him on his lap with the next Yagus (M. II, II, 21), with the next (three) (verses--II, 11, 22; 12, 1. 2--one by one) he addresses the child, kisses him on his head, and murmurs (the third verse) into his right ear.
And he gives him a Nakshatra name.

15.s: madhu ghṛtamiti saṃsṛjya tasmin darbheṇa hiraṇyaṃ niṣṭarkya badhvāvadāyottarairmantraiḥ kumāraṃ prāśayitvottarābhiḥ pañcabhissnāpayitvā dadhi ghṛtamiti saṃsṛjya kāṃsyena pṛṣadājyaṃ vyāhṛtībhiroṅgāracaturthābhiḥ kumāraṃ prāśayitvādbhiśśeṣaṃ saṃsṛjya goṣṭhe ninayet |
15.d: मधु घृतमिति संसृज्य तस्मिन् दर्भेण हिरण्यं निष्टर्क्य बध्वावदायोत्तरैर्मन्त्रैः कुमारं प्राशयित्वोत्तराभिः पञ्चभिस्स्नापयित्वा दधि घृतमिति संसृज्य कांस्येन पृषदाज्यं व्याहृतीभिरोङ्गारचतुर्थाभिः कुमारं प्राशयित्वाद्भिश्शेषं संसृज्य गोष्ठे निनयेत् ।
15.e: He pours together honey and ghee; into this (mixture) he dips a piece of gold which he has tied with a noose to a Darbha blade. With the next (three) formulas (II, 12, 3-5) he gives the boy (by means of the piece of gold, some of the mixture) to eat. With the next five (verses, II, 12, 6-10) he bathes him. Then he pours curds and ghee together and gives him this (mixture which is called) 'sprinkled butter' (prishadagya) to eat out of a brass vessel, with the Vyahritis to which the syllable 'Om' is added as the fourth (II, 12, 11-14). The remainder he should mix with water and pour out in a cow-stable.

15.s: uttarayā māturupastha ādhāyottarayā dakṣiṇaṃ stanaṃ pratidhāpyottarābhyāṃ pṛthivīmabhimṛśyottareṇa yajuṣā saṃviṣṭam |
15.d: उत्तरया मातुरुपस्थ आधायोत्तरया दक्षिणं स्तनं प्रतिधाप्योत्तराभ्यां पृथिवीमभिमृश्योत्तरेण यजुषा संविष्टम् ।
15.e: With the next (verse, M. II, 13, 1) he places (the child) in the mother's lap; with the next (II, 13, 2) he causes her to give him her right breast; with the next two (verses, II, 13, 3. 4) he touches the earth, and after (the child) has been laid down, (he touches him) with the next (formula, II, 13, 5).

15.s: uttareṇa yajuṣā śirasta udkumbhaṃ nidhāya sarṣapān phalīkaraṇamiśrānañjalinottaraistristriḥ pratisvāhākāraṃ hutvā saṃśāsti praviṣṭe praviṣṭa eva tūṣṇīmagnāvāvapateti |
15.d: उत्तरेण यजुषा शिरस्त उद्कुम्भं निधाय सर्षपान् फलीकरणमिश्रानञ्जलिनोत्तरैस्त्रिस्त्रिः प्रतिस्वाहाकारं हुत्वा संशास्ति प्रविष्टे प्रविष्ट एव तूष्णीमग्नावावपतेति ।
15.e: With the next Yagus (II, 13, 6) he places a water-pot at (the child's) head, sacrifices mustard seeds and rice-chaff with his joined hands three times with each of the next (formulas, II, 13, 7-14, 2), repeating each time the word Svaha, and says (to the people who are accustomed to enter the room in which his wife lies), 'Whenever you enter, strew silently (mustard seeds with rice-chaff) on the fire.'
This is to be done until the ten days (after the child's birth) have elapsed.

15.s: daśamyāmutthitāyāṃ snātāyāṃ putrasya nāma dadhāti pitā māteti |
15.d: दशम्यामुत्थितायां स्नातायां पुत्रस्य नाम दधाति पिता मातेति ।
15.e: On the tenth day, after (the mother) has risen and taken a bath, he gives a name to the son. The father and the mother (should pronounce that name first).

15.s: dvyakṣaraṃ caturakṣaraṃ vā nāmapūrvamākhyātottaraṃ dīrghābhiniṣṭhānāntaṃ ghoṣavadādyantarantastham |
15.d: द्व्यक्षरं चतुरक्षरं वा नामपूर्वमाख्यातोत्तरं दीर्घाभिनिष्ठानान्तं घोषवदाद्यन्तरन्तस्थम् ।

15.s: api vā yasmin svityupasargassyāt taddhi pratiṣṭhitamiti hi brāhmaṇam |
15.d: अपि वा यस्मिन् स्वित्युपसर्गस्स्यात् तद्धि प्रतिष्ठितमिति हि ब्राह्मणम् ।

15.e: A girl's name should have an odd number of syllables.

15.s: pravāsādetya putrasyottarābhyāmabhimantraṇaṃ mūrdhanyavaghrāṇaṃ dakṣiṇe karṇa uttarān mantrān japet |
15.d: प्रवासादेत्य पुत्रस्योत्तराभ्यामभिमन्त्रणं मूर्धन्यवघ्राणं दक्षिणे कर्ण उत्तरान् मन्त्रान् जपेत् ।
15.e: When (the father) returns from a journey, he should address the child and kiss him on his head with the next two (verses, M. II, 14, 3. 4), and should murmur the next Mantras (II, 14, 5) into his right ear.
With the next Yagus (II, 14, 6) he addresses a daughter (when returning from a journey).

16.s: janmano 'dhi ṣaṣṭhe māsi brāhmaṇān bhojayitvā'śiṣo vācayitvā dadhi madhu ghṛtamodanamiti saṃsṛjyottarairmantraiḥ kumāraṃ prāśayet |
16.d: जन्मनो ऽधि षष्ठे मासि ब्राह्मणान् भोजयित्वाऽशिषो वाचयित्वा दधि मधु घृतमोदनमिति संसृज्योत्तरैर्मन्त्रैः कुमारं प्राशयेत् ।
16.e: In the sixth month after the child's birth he serves food to Brahmanas and causes them to pronounce auspicious wishes; then he should pour together curds, honey, ghee, and boiled rice, and should give (the mixture) to the boy to eat, with the next (four) Mantras (II, 14, 7-10);
(He should feed him) with partridge, according to some (teachers).

16.d: जन्मनो ऽधि तृतीये वर्षे चौलं पुनर्वस्वोः ।
16.e: In the third year after his birth the Kaula (or tonsure is performed) under (the Nakshatra of) the two Punarvasus.
Brahmanas are entertained with food as at the initiation (Upanayana).
The putting (of wood) on the fire, &c. (is performed) as at the Simantonnayana.

He makes (the boy) sit down to the west of the fire, facing the east, combs his hair silently with a porcupine's quill that has three white spots, with three Darbha blades, and with a bunch of unripe Udumbara fruits; and he arranges the locks in the fashion of his ancestral Rishis,
Or according to their family custom.
The ceremonies beginning with the pouring together of (warm and cold) water and ending with the putting down of the hair are the same (as above; comp. M. II, 14, 11).
He puts down the razor after having washed it off.
The ceremony is (repeated) three days with the (same razor). (Then) the rite is finished.
(The father) gives an optional gift (to the Brahmana who has assisted).
The Godana (or the ceremony of shaving the beard, is performed) in the sixteenth year, in exactly the same way or optionally under another constellation.
Or he may perform the Godana sacred to Agni.
Some prescribe the keeping of a vow through one year in connection with the Godana.
The difference (between the Kaula and the Godana) is that (at the Godana) the whole hair is shaven (without leaving the locks).
According to the followers of the Sama-veda he should 'touch water.'

17.e: The ground for building a house should be inclined towards the south-west. He elevates the surface and sweeps (the earth) with a broom of Palasa wood or of Sami wood, with the next (verse, M. II, 15, 1), in the same (south-west) direction;
In the same way three times.

17.s: kḷptamuttarayābhimṛśya pradakṣiṇaṃ sthūṇāgartān khānayitvābhyantaraṃ pāṃsūnudupyottarābhyāṃ dakṣiṇāṃ dvārasthūṇāmavadadhāti |
17.d: कॢप्तमुत्तरयाभिमृश्य प्रदक्षिणं स्थूणागर्तान् खानयित्वाभ्यन्तरं पांसूनुदुप्योत्तराभ्यां दक्षिणां द्वारस्थूणामवदधाति ।
17.e: He touches the ground, which has thus been prepared, with the next (verse, II, 15, 2). Then he has the pits for the posts dug from left to right, throws the earth (from the pits) towards the inside (of the building-ground), and erects the right doorpost with the next two (verses, M. II, 15, 3. 4)
In the same way the other (door-post).

Having erected after (the door-posts) the other (posts) in the same order in which (the pits) have been dug, he recites the next Yagus (II, 15, 5) over the ridge-pole when it is placed (on the posts),
The next (six) (Yagus formulas, II, 15, 6-11) over the (house when it is) finished, according to the characteristics contained in the single formulas.

17.s: pālāśaṃ śamīmayaṃ vedhmamādīpyottarayāgnimuddhṛtyottareṇa yajuṣāgāraṃ prapādyottarapūrvadeśe 'gārasyottarayāgniṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati |
17.d: पालाशं शमीमयं वेध्ममादीप्योत्तरयाग्निमुद्धृत्योत्तरेण यजुषागारं प्रपाद्योत्तरपूर्वदेशे ऽगारस्योत्तरयाग्निं प्रतिष्ठापयति ।
17.e: He sets a piece of Palasa wood or of Sami wood on fire, takes the fire up (in a dish) with the next verse (II, 15, 12), carries it to the house with the next Yagus (II, 15, 13), and places the fire in the north-eastern part of the house with the next (II, 15, 14).
The place for the water-barrel is to the south of that spot.

17.s: tasminviṣūcīnāgrāndarbhānsaṃstīrya teṣūttarayā vrīhiyavān nyupya tatrodadhānaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati |
17.d: तस्मिन्विषूचीनाग्रान्दर्भान्संस्तीर्य तेषूत्तरया व्रीहियवान् न्युप्य तत्रोदधानं प्रतिष्ठापयति ।
17.e: He strews there Darbha grass, so that its points are turned in every direction, pours rice and barley-grains over the (grass) with the next (verse, II, 15, 15), and thereon he places the water-barrel.
With the next (Yagus, II, 15, 16) he pours four potfuls of water into it.
If (the barrel) breaks, he recites the next (verse, II, 15, 17) over it.

After the ceremonies from the putting of wood on the fire down to the Agyabhaga oblations have been performed, he offers the (four) oblations (indicated by the) next (Mantras; II, 15, 18-21); then he enters upon the performance of the Gaya and following oblations.

17.s: pariṣecanāntaṃ kṛtvottareṇa yajuṣodakumbhena triḥ pradakṣiṇamantarato 'gāraṃ niveśanaṃ vā pariṣicya brāhmaṇān bhojayedapūpaissaktubhirodaneneti |
17.d: परिषेचनान्तं कृत्वोत्तरेण यजुषोदकुम्भेन त्रिः प्रदक्षिणमन्तरतो ऽगारं निवेशनं वा परिषिच्य ब्राह्मणान् भोजयेदपूपैस्सक्तुभिरोदनेनेति ।
17.e: Having performed (the rites) down to the sprinkling (of water) round (the fire), he should sprinkle (water) with a water-pot around the house or the resting-place on the inside, with the next Yagus (II, 15, 22) three times from left to right; then he should serve cakes, flour, and boiled rice to the Brahmanas.

18.s: śvagrahahītaṃ kumāraṃ tapoyukto jālena pracchādya kaṃsaṃ kiṅkiṇiṃ vā hrādayannadvāreṇa sabhāṃ prapādya sabhāyā madhye 'dhidevanamuddhatyāvokṣyākṣānnyupyākṣeṣūttānaṃ nipātya dadhnā lavaṇamiśreṇāñjalinottarairavokṣetprātarmadhyandine sāyam |
18.d: श्वग्रहहीतं कुमारं तपोयुक्तो जालेन प्रच्छाद्य कंसं किङ्किणिं वा ह्रादयन्नद्वारेण सभां प्रपाद्य सभाया मध्ये ऽधिदेवनमुद्धत्यावोक्ष्याक्षान्न्युप्याक्षेषूत्तानं निपात्य दध्ना लवणमिश्रेणाञ्जलिनोत्तरैरवोक्षेत्प्रातर्मध्यन्दिने सायम् ।
18.e: When a boy is attacked by the dog-demon (i.e. epilepsy), (the father or another performer of the ceremony), having devoted himself to austerities [paragraph continues] (such as fasting), covers him with a net. Then he causes a gong to be beaten or a bell to be rung, takes (the boy) by another way than the door into the gambling-hall, raises (the earth in the middle of the hall) at the place in which they gamble, sprinkles it (with water), casts the dice, lays (the boy) on his back on the dice, and besprinkles him with his joined hands with curds and salt, with the next (eleven) (formulas, II, 16, 1-11), in the morning, at noon, and at night.

18.s: śaṅkhinaṃ kumāraṃ tapoyukta uttarābhyāmabhimantryottarayodakumbhena śirasto 'vanayetprātarmadhyandine sāyam |
18.d: शङ्खिनं कुमारं तपोयुक्त उत्तराभ्यामभिमन्त्र्योत्तरयोदकुम्भेन शिरस्तो ऽवनयेत्प्रातर्मध्यन्दिने सायम् ।
18.e: Over a boy who suffers from the 'Sankha' disease, (the father, &c.) having devoted himself to austerities, should recite the next two (verses, II, 16, 12. 13), and should pour (water) on his head with a water-pot with the next (verse, II, 16, 14), in the morning, at noon, and at night.
On the day of the full moon of (the month) Sravana after sunset a Sthalipaka (is offered).

After the ceremonies down to the Agyabhaga oblations have been performed in the same way as at the fortnightly sacrifices, he sacrifices of the Sthalipaka, and with each of the next (formulas, II, 16, 15-17) he offers with his joined hands Kimsuka flowers.
With the next (three) verses (II, 17, 1-3) (he offers) pieces of Aragvadha wood (Cathartocarpus fistula);
Then the Agya oblations (indicated by the) next (Mantras, II, 17, 4-7).
Then he enters upon the performance of the Gaya and following oblations.

18.s: pariṣecanāntaṃ kṛtvā vāgyatassaṃbhārānādāya prācīmudīcīṃ vā diśamupaniṣkramya sthaṇḍilaṃ kalpayitvā tatra prācīrudīcīśca tistrastistro lekhā likhitvādbhirupaninīya tāsūttarayā saktūnnivapati |
18.d: परिषेचनान्तं कृत्वा वाग्यतस्संभारानादाय प्राचीमुदीचीं वा दिशमुपनिष्क्रम्य स्थण्डिलं कल्पयित्वा तत्र प्राचीरुदीचीश्च तिस्त्रस्तिस्त्रो लेखा लिखित्वाद्भिरुपनिनीय तासूत्तरया सक्तून्निवपति ।
18.e: Having performed (the rites) down to the sprinkling (of water) round (the fire), he silently takes the objects required (for the rites which he is going to perform), goes out in an easterly or northerly direction, prepares a raised surface, draws on it three lines directed towards the east and three towards the north, pours water on the (lines), and lays (an offering of) flour (for the serpents) on them, with the next (formula, II, 17, 8).

18.s: uttarairupasthāyāpaḥ pariṣicyāpratīkṣastūṣṇīmetyā paśveta padetyetābhyāmudakumbhena triḥ pradakṣiṇamantarato 'gāraṃ niveśanaṃ vā pariṣicya brāhmaṇān bhojayet |
18.d: उत्तरैरुपस्थायापः परिषिच्याप्रतीक्षस्तूष्णीमेत्या पश्वेत पदेत्येताभ्यामुदकुम्भेन त्रिः प्रदक्षिणमन्तरतो ऽगारं निवेशनं वा परिषिच्य ब्राह्मणान् भोजयेत् ।

19.e: The unground grain (which is left over, see above, VII, 18, 11) they give to the boys to eat.

19.s: evamata ūrdhva yadaśanīyasya saktūnāṃ vaitaṃ baliṃ haredāmārgaśīrṣyāḥ |
19.d: एवमत ऊर्ध्व यदशनीयस्य सक्तूनां वैतं बलिं हरेदामार्गशीर्ष्याः ।
19.e: Let him repeat in the same way this Bali-offering of whatever food he has got or of flour, from that day to full moon of (the month) Margasirsha.
On the day of the full moon of Margasirsha after sunset a Sthalipaka (is offered as above, VII, 18, 5).
In the Mantra for the Bali-offering he changes (the word 'I shall offer' into) 'I have offered.'
Then he does not offer (the Bali) any longer.
(Now follows) the Agrayana sacrifice (or partaking of the first-fruits) of one who has not set up the (Srauta) fires.

19.s: navānāṃ sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvā'grayaṇadevatābhyaḥ sviṣṭakṛccaturthābhyo hutvā taṇḍulānāṃ mukhaṃ pūrayitvā gīrtvā'camyaudanapiṇḍaṃ saṃvṛttyottareṇa yajuṣāgārastūpa udviddhet |
19.d: नवानां स्थालीपाकं श्रपयित्वाऽग्रयणदेवताभ्यः स्विष्टकृच्चतुर्थाभ्यो हुत्वा तण्डुलानां मुखं पूरयित्वा गीर्त्वाऽचम्यौदनपिण्डं संवृत्त्योत्तरेण यजुषागारस्तूप उद्विद्धेत् ।
19.e: He prepares a Sthalipaka of the fresh fruits, sacrifices to the deities of the (Srauta) Agrayana sacrifice with (Agni) Svishtakrit as the fourth, fills his mouth with grains, swallows them, sips water, forms a lump of the boiled (sacrificial) food, and throws it up with the next Yagus (II, 18, 1) to the summit of the house.

19.s: uttareṇa yajuṣā pratyavaruhyottarairdakṣiṇaiḥ pārśvaiḥ navasvastare saṃviśanti |
19.d: उत्तरेण यजुषा प्रत्यवरुह्योत्तरैर्दक्षिणैः पार्श्वैः नवस्वस्तरे संविशन्ति ।
19.e: With the next Yagus (II, 18, 2) they 'redescend' (or take as their sleeping-place a layer of straw instead of the high bedsteads which they have used before). With the next Yagus formulas (II, 18, 3-7) they lie down on a new layer (of straw) on their right sides,

19.d: दक्षिणतः पितोत्तरा मातैवमवशिष्टानां ज्येष्ठो ज्येष्ठो ऽनन्तरः ।
19.e: The father to the south, the mother to the north (of him), and so the others, one after the other from the eldest to the youngest.
After he has arisen, he touches the earth with the next two (verses, II, 18, 8. 9).
In the same way the lying down, &c., is repeated thrice.

19.s: īśānāya sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvā kṣaitrapatyaṃ ca prācīmudīcīṃ vā diśamupaniṣkramya sthaṇḍilaṃ kalpayitvāgnerupasamādhānādi |
19.d: ईशानाय स्थालीपाकं श्रपयित्वा क्षैत्रपत्यं च प्राचीमुदीचीं वा दिशमुपनिष्क्रम्य स्थण्डिलं कल्पयित्वाग्नेरुपसमाधानादि ।
19.e: Having prepared a Sthalipaka for Lana and one for Kshetrapati, he goes out in an easterly or northerly direction, prepares a raised surface, (and then follow the ceremonies) beginning with the putting of wood on the fire.
To the west of the fire he builds two huts.

20.e: With the next (verse, II, 18, 10) he has the Isana led to the southern (hut),
With worldly words the 'bountiful goddess' to the northern (hut),
To the middle (between the two huts) the 'conqueror.'

20.s: yathoḍhamudakāni pradāya trīnodanān kalpayitvāgnimabhyānīyottaraikupasparśayitvā uttarairyathāsvamodanebhyo hutvā sarvatassamavadāyottareṇa yajuṣāgniṃ sviṣṭakṛtam |
20.d: यथोढमुदकानि प्रदाय त्रीनोदनान् कल्पयित्वाग्निमभ्यानीयोत्तरैकुपस्पर्शयित्वा उत्तरैर्यथास्वमोदनेभ्यो हुत्वा सर्वतस्समवदायोत्तरेण यजुषाग्निं स्विष्टकृतम् ।
20.e: He gives them water to drink in the same order in which they have been led (to their places), takes three portions of boiled rice (from the Sthalipaka prepared for Isana), takes (these portions of rice) to the fire, makes (the three gods) touch them with the next (formulas, II, 18, II-13), sacrifices of these portions, to each god of the portion which belongs to him, with the next (formulas, II, 18, 14-30), cuts off (Avadanas) from all (portions), and sacrifices with the next Yagus (II, 18, 31) to Agni Svishtakrit.

20.s: uttareṇa yajuṣopasthāyottaraissahaudanāni parṇānyekaikena dve dve datvā daśa devasenābhyo daśottarābhyaḥ |
20.d: उत्तरेण यजुषोपस्थायोत्तरैस्सहौदनानि पर्णान्येकैकेन द्वे द्वे दत्वा दश देवसेनाभ्यो दशोत्तराभ्यः ।
20.e: Having worshipped (the god Isana) with the next Yagus (II, 18, 32), he distributes with the next (formulas, II, 18, 33-39) leaves together with portions of boiled rice, two (leaves) with each (Yagus), then ten to the divine hosts (II, 18, 40), and ten to the (divine hosts) that follow (and are referred to in the next Yagus, II, 18, 41).
With the next (formulas, II, 18, 42-45) he does the same as before (i.e. he distributes two leaves with each Mantra).

20.s: odanapiṇḍaṃ saṃvṛtya parṇapuṭe 'vadhāyottareṇa yajuṣā vṛkṣa āsajati |
20.d: ओदनपिण्डं संवृत्य पर्णपुटे ऽवधायोत्तरेण यजुषा वृक्ष आसजति ।
20.e: Having formed a lump of boiled rice, he puts it into a basket of leaves, and with the next Yagus (II, 18, 46) hangs it up on a tree.
Here he should murmur the Rudra texts (Taitt. Samh. IV, 5),

20.s: abhita etamagniṃ gāssthāpayati yathainā dhūmaḥ prāpnuyāt |
20.d: अभित एतमग्निं गास्स्थापयति यथैना धूमः प्राप्नुयात् ।
20.e: He places his cows around the fire so that the smoke (of the sacrifice) may reach them.
With his firmly shut fist full of Darbha grass he besprinkles (them) with scents; the bull first.

20.d: गवां मर्गे ऽनग्नौ क्षेत्रस्य पतिं यजते ।
20.e: He should perform a sacrifice to Kshetrapati, without a fire, in the path used by his cows.
He has (the Kshetrapati) led to his place in the same way as the Isana (see above, Sutra 1).

20.s: caturṣu saptasu vā parṇeṣu nāmādeśaṃ dadhāti |
20.d: चतुर्षु सप्तसु वा पर्णेषु नामादेशं दधाति ।
20.e: He puts (portions of boiled rice) into four or seven leaves, naming (the god).
Let him sacrifice quickly; the god has a strong digestion (?).
With the next two (verses, II, 18, 47. 48) he does worship (to Kshetrapati).
The Sthalipaka (belonging to Isana) he gives to the Brahmanas to eat;
That belonging to Kshetrapati his uterine relations eat,
Or as is the custom in their family.

21.e: The times for the monthly Sraddha are in the second fortnight (of the month), as they are stated.

Let him feed, without regard of (worldly) purposes, pure Brahmanas, versed in the Mantras, who are not connected with himself by consanguinity or by their Gotra or by the Mantras (such as his teacher or his pupils), an odd number, at least three.
He makes oblations of the food (prepared for the Brahmanas) with the next (verses, II, 19,1-7);
Then the Agya oblations (indicated by the) next (Mantras, II, 19, 8-13).
Or invertedly (i.e. he offers Agya with the verses referred to in Sutra 3, and food with those referred to in Sutra 4).
Let him touch the whole (food) with the next (formulas, II, 19, 14-16).
Or the (single) prepared (portions of food destined) for the single Brahmanas.
Having caused them with the next (formula, II, 20, 1) to touch (the food, he gives it to them to eat).

21.s: bhuktavato 'nuvrajya pradakṣiṇīkṛtya dvaidhaṃ dakṣiṇāgrān darbhān saṃstīrya teṣūttarairapo datvottarairdakṣiṇāpavargān piṇḍāndatvā pūrvavaduttarairapo datvottarairupasthāyottarayodapātreṇa triḥprasavyaṃ pariṣicya nyubjya pātrāṇyuttaraṃ yajuranavānaṃ tryavarārghyamāvartayitvā prokṣyapātrāṇi dvandvamabhyudāhṛtya sarvatassamavadāyottareṇa yajuṣā śeṣasya grāsavarārghya prāśnīyāt |
21.d: भुक्तवतो ऽनुव्रज्य प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य द्वैधं दक्षिणाग्रान् दर्भान् संस्तीर्य तेषूत्तरैरपो दत्वोत्तरैर्दक्षिणापवर्गान् पिण्डान्दत्वा पूर्ववदुत्तरैरपो दत्वोत्तरैरुपस्थायोत्तरयोदपात्रेण त्रिःप्रसव्यं परिषिच्य न्युब्ज्य पात्राण्युत्तरं यजुरनवानं त्र्यवरार्घ्यमावर्तयित्वा प्रोक्ष्यपात्राणि द्वन्द्वमभ्युदाहृत्य सर्वतस्समवदायोत्तरेण यजुषा शेषस्य ग्रासवरार्घ्य प्राश्नीयात् ।
21.e: When they have eaten (and gone away), he goes after them, circumambulates them, turning his right side towards them, spreads out southward-pointed Darbha grass in two different layers, pours water on it with the next (formulas, II, 20, 2-7), distributes the Pindas, ending in the south, with the next (formulas, II, 20, 8-13), pours out water as before with the next (formulas, 14-19), worships (the ancestors) with the next (formulas, II, 20, 20-23), sprinkles with the next (verse, 24) water three times from right to left round (the Pindas) with a water-pot, besprinkles the vessels, which are turned upside down, repeating the next Yagus (25) at least three times without taking breath, sets up the vessels two by two, cuts off (Avadanas) from all (portions of food), and eats of the remains at least one morsel with the next Yagus (26).

21.s: yā māghyāḥ paurṇamāsyā uparidvyahyaṣṭakā tasyāmaṣṭamī jyeṣṭhayā sampadyate tāmekāṣṭaketyācakṣate |
21.d: या माघ्याः पौर्णमास्या उपरिद्व्यह्यष्टका तस्यामष्टमी ज्येष्ठया सम्पद्यते तामेकाष्टकेत्याचक्षते ।
21.e: Of the dark fortnight that follows after the full moon of Magha, the eighth day falls under (the constellation of) Gyeshtha: this day is called Ekashtaka.
In the evening before that day (he performs) the preparatory ceremony.
He bakes a cake of four cups (of rice).
(The cake is prepared) in eight dishes (like a Purodasa), according to some (teachers).

22.e: After the ceremonies down to the Agyabhaga oblations have been performed in the same way as at the fortnightly sacrifices, he makes with his joined hands oblations of the cake with the next (verse, II, 20, 27).
The rest (of the cake) he makes ready, divides (it) into eight parts and offers it to the Brahmanas.
On the following day he touches a cow with a Darbha blade, with the words, 'I touch thee agreeable to the Fathers.'

22.s: tūṣṇīṃ pañcājyāhutīrhutvā tasyai vapāṃ śrapayitvopastīrṇābhighāritāṃ madhyamenāntamena vā palāśaparṇenottarayā juhoti |
22.d: तूष्णीं पञ्चाज्याहुतीर्हुत्वा तस्यै वपां श्रपयित्वोपस्तीर्णाभिघारितां मध्यमेनान्तमेन वा पलाशपर्णेनोत्तरया जुहोति ।
22.e: Having silently offered five Agya oblations, and having cooked, the omentum of the (cow), and performed the 'spreading under' and the sprinkling over (of Agya), he sacrifices (the omentum) with the next (verse, II, 20, 28) with a Palasa leaf from the middle or the end (of the stalk).
(He sacrifices) boiled rice together with the meat (of the cow) with the next (verses, II, 20, 29-35),
Food prepared of meal with the next (verse, II, 21, 1),
Then the Agya oblations (indicated by the) next (Mantras, II, 21, 2-9).
(The rites) from the Svishtakrit down to the offering of the Pindas are the same (as at the Sraddha).
Some (teachers) prescribe the Pinda offering for the day after the Ashtaka.
Here (follows) another (way for celebrating the Ashtaka sacrifice). He sacrifices curds with his joined hands in the same way as the cake.

22.s: ata eva yathārtha māṃsaṃ śiṣṭvā śvobhūte 'nvaṣṭakām |
22.d: अत एव यथार्थ मांसं शिष्ट्वा श्वोभूते ऽन्वष्टकाम् ।
22.e: Having left over from the meat of the (cow, see above, 3. 4) as much as is required, on the day after (the Ashtaka) (he performs) the rite of the Anvashtaka.
This rite has been explained in the description of the monthly Sraddha.
If he goes out in order to beg for something, let him murmur the next (Mantras, II, 21, 10-16) and then state his desire.

22.s: rathaṃ labdhvā yojayitvā prāñcamavasthāpyottarayā rathacakre abhimṛśati pakṣasī vā |
22.d: रथं लब्ध्वा योजयित्वा प्राञ्चमवस्थाप्योत्तरया रथचक्रे अभिमृशति पक्षसी वा ।
22.e: If he has obtained a chariot, he has the horses put to it, lets it face the east, and touches with the next (verse, II, 21, 17) the two wheels of the chariot or the two side-pieces.

22.s: uttareṇa yajuṣādhīruhyottarayā prācīmudīcīṃ vā diśamabhiprayāya yathārtha yāyāt |
22.d: उत्तरेण यजुषाधीरुह्योत्तरया प्राचीमुदीचीं वा दिशमभिप्रयाय यथार्थ यायात् ।
22.e: With the next Yagus (II, 21, 18) he should mount, and drive with the next (verse, II, 21, 19) towards the east or north, and should then drive off on his business.
Let him mount a horse with the next (formulas, II, 21, 20-30),
An elephant with the next (formula, II, 21, 31).
If any harm is done him by these two (beasts), let him touch the earth as indicated above.
If he is going to a dispute, he takes the parasol and the staff in his left hand.

23.e: Having sacrificed, with his right hand, a fist full of chaff with the next (verse, II, 21, 32), he should go away and murmur the next (verse, 33).
Over an angry person let him recite the two next (formulas, II, 22, 1. 2); then his anger will be appeased.

23.s: asaṃbhavepsuḥ pareṣāṃ sthūlāḍhārikājīvacūrṇāni kārayitvottarayā suptāyāssambādha upavapet |
23.d: असंभवेप्सुः परेषां स्थूलाढारिकाजीवचूर्णानि कारयित्वोत्तरया सुप्तायास्सम्बाध उपवपेत् ।
23.e: One who wishes that his wife should not be touched by other men, should have big living centipedes ground to powder, and should insert (that powder) with the next (formula, II, 22, 3), while she is sleeping, into her secret parts.
For success (in the generation of children) let him wash (his wife) with the urine of a red-brown cow.

23.s: siddhyarthe yadasya gṛhe paṇyaṃ syāttata uttarayā juhuyāt |
23.d: सिद्ध्यर्थे यदस्य गृहे पण्यं स्यात्तत उत्तरया जुहुयात् ।
23.e: For success (in trade) let him sacrifice with the next (verse--II, 22, 4--some portion) from the articles of trade which he has in his house.

23.s: yaṃ kāmayeta nāyaṃ macchidyeteti jīvaviṣāṇe svaṃ mūtramānīya suptamuttarābhyāṃ triḥ prasavyaṃ pariṣiñcet |
23.d: यं कामयेत नायं मच्छिद्येतेति जीवविषाणे स्वं मूत्रमानीय सुप्तमुत्तराभ्यां त्रिः प्रसव्यं परिषिञ्चेत् ।
23.e: If he wishes that somebody be not estranged from him, let him pour his own urine into the horn of a living animal, and sprinkle (it) with the next two (verses, II, 22, 5. 6) three times from right to left around (the person) while he is sleeping.

23.s: yena pathā dāsakarmakarāḥ palāyeran tasminniṇvānyupasamādhāyottarā āhutījuhuyāt |
23.d: येन पथा दासकर्मकराः पलायेरन् तस्मिन्निण्वान्युपसमाधायोत्तरा आहुतीजुहुयात् ।
23.e: In a path which servants or labourers use to run away, he should put plates (used for protecting the hands when holding a hot sacrificial pan) on (a fire), and should offer the oblations (indicated by the) next (Mantras, II, 22, 7-10).

23.s: yadyenaṃ vṛkṣāt phalamabhinipatedvayo vābhivikṣipedavarṣatarkye vā bindurabhinipatettaduttarairyathāliṅgaṃ prakṣālayīta |
23.d: यद्येनं वृक्षात् फलमभिनिपतेद्वयो वाभिविक्षिपेदवर्षतर्क्ये वा बिन्दुरभिनिपतेत्तदुत्तरैर्यथालिङ्गं प्रक्षालयीत ।
23.e: If a fruit falls on him from a tree, or a bird befouls him, or a drop of water falls on him when no rain is expected, he should wipe that off with the next (Mantras, II, 22, 11-13), according to the characteristics (contained in these Mantras).

23.s: āgārasthūṇāvirohaṇe madhuna upaveśane kuptvāṃ kapotapadadarśane 'mātyānāṃ śarīrareṣaṇe 'nyeṣu cādbhutotpāteṣvamāvāsyāyāṃ niśāyāṃ yatrāpāṃ na śṛṇuyāttadagnerupasamādhānādyājyabhāgānta uttarā āhutīrhutvā jayādi pratipadyate |
23.d: आगारस्थूणाविरोहणे मधुन उपवेशने कुप्त्वां कपोतपददर्शने ऽमात्यानां शरीररेषणे ऽन्येषु चाद्भुतोत्पातेष्वमावास्यायां निशायां यत्रापां न शृणुयात्तदग्नेरुपसमाधानाद्याज्यभागान्त उत्तरा आहुतीर्हुत्वा जयादि प्रतिपद्यते ।
23.e: If a post of his house puts forth shoots, or if honey is made in his house (by bees), or if the footprint of a dove is seen on the hearth, or if diseases arise in his household, or in the case of other miracles or prodigies, let him perform in the new-moon night, at dead of night, at a place where he does not hear the noise of water, the rites from the putting (of wood) on the fire down to the Agyabhaga oblations, and let him offer the oblations (indicated in the) next (Mantras, II, 22, 14-23), and enter upon the performance of the Gaya and following oblations.

23.s: pariṣecanāntaṃ kṛtvābhimṛtebhya uttarayā dakṣiṇato 'śmānaṃ paridhiṃ dadhāti dadhāti |
23.d: परिषेचनान्तं कृत्वाभिमृतेभ्य उत्तरया दक्षिणतो ऽश्मानं परिधिं दधाति दधाति ।
23.e: Having performed (the ceremonies) down to the sprinkling (of water) round (the fire), he puts up towards the south with the next (verse, II, 22, 24) a stone as a barrier for those among whom a death has occurred.
